title: Man shot and killed by police near Cold Lake; police dog injured
article: A man is dead after being shot by an RCMP officer near Cold Lake on Sunday - the second fatal shooting involving Alberta RCMP officers in the province in a span of three days.
On Monday, RCMP revealed an officer had shot and killed an unidentified man during a Sunday evening foot chase near Ardmore, a hamlet 260 kilometres northeast of Edmonton.
The incident began at 6:50 p.m. when Cold Lake RCMP received a call about a "dispute" inside a vehicle. RCMP began a search, calling in a police service dog team to track the suspect.

After a while, officers found the man and a "confrontation" ensued that ended with an officer firing their weapon. The suspect suffered life-threatening injuries and died at the scene despite emergency first aid provided by the officers.
The police service dog was taken to a veterinarian after suffering minor injuries.
The Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT), the province's police watchdog, is investigating the man's death.
Meantime, ASIRT is investigating the killing of a 29-year-old man in High Prairie on Friday, shot to death by police.
ASIRT said in a Monday news release two RCMP officers fired at Lionel Ernest Grey, 29, of the Gift Lake Metis Settlement, and he died from his injuries. The RCMP initially did not say how he died.
The manhunt began after Grey allegedly failed to pull over for a traffic stop on Thursday.
Police and Grey exchanged gunfire twice.

On Thursday, the RCMP, including a police dog team, tracked Grey down in a bush and they shot at each other, ASIRT says. A police dog was killed in the exchange of gunfire - police haven't said who shot the dog - but no one else was injured during that altercation.
Officers found Grey twice more over the course of the day and gave him verbal commands but he was not captured, according to ASIRT.
On Friday around 11:45 a.m., Grey appeared at a "containment point" in a ditch on the west side of Range Road 170, about two kilometres north of Township Road 770.
Two officers got out of a marked police vehicle and shot at Grey, ASIRT says. Grey fell into the grass, fatally wounded. Paramedics attempted to treat him but he died on site.
A loaded semi-automatic .22 calibre rifle and a range finder was found at the scene, ASIRT says.
The RCMP is continuing its investigation of Grey while ASIRT investigates the actions of police.
